## When each skill applies

### `break-down-tasks`

Use when the user asks to "break this down into tasks", "split this spec into work items", "plan the work", "estimate this" or "what order should we build this in", and an approved spec or large change exists. Do not use for a change under about one hour, or while the spec is unsettled.

### `clarify-requirements`

Use when the user gives a vague request such as "make it better", "add export" or "support teams", or asks "what are we actually building" or "what should I ask first". Produces confirmed facts, labelled assumptions and at most five blocking questions. Do not use when the request already has testable acceptance criteria, for a bug with a reproduction, or for slowness (use investigate-performance).

### `debug-from-evidence`

Use when the user says "this test is failing", "find the bug", "why is this crashing", "it fails sometimes" or "this worked yesterday". Builds a reproduction, tests ranked hypotheses by observation and fixes the root cause. Do not use when the cause is already known (use test-first-change) or for slowness (use investigate-performance).

### `design-http-api`

Use when the user asks to "design an API", "add an endpoint", "review this OpenAPI spec", "add pagination" or "design the webhook", for an HTTP or JSON API that other programs depend on. Do not use for internal function signatures, GraphQL or RPC schema design, or user-interface work.

### `give-and-receive-code-review`

Use when the user says "review this PR", "review my changes", "give feedback on this diff" or "reply to these review comments". Covers labelling findings, proving blockers and replying with evidence. Do not use for the checks you run on your own work before committing, a whole-system security audit (use review-security-surface), or settling design before any code exists.

### `investigate-performance`

Use when the user says "this is slow", "why is this endpoint slow", "reduce the latency", "memory keeps growing" or "make it faster", and the cause must be located and proven. Do not use for optimization without a measured problem, or for wrong results (use debug-from-evidence).

### `plan-database-migration`

Use when the user asks to "add a column", "rename a table", "backfill this data", "add an index" or "plan this migration" on a live database. Do not use for disposable development databases, ORM model edits with no schema effect, or read-only queries.

### `refactor-without-behavior-change`

Use when the user asks to "refactor this", "clean this up", "extract this into a function", "rename this everywhere" or "deduplicate this" and behavior must stay identical. Do not use when behavior is meant to change (do that in a separate change), or when no test or other check can observe current behavior and none can be added.

### `release-with-rollback`

Use when the user asks to "ship this", "deploy to production", "plan the release", "roll this out gradually" or "how do we roll back", for a change users would notice failing. Do not use for local or throwaway environments, or for documentation-only changes.

### `review-security-surface`

Use when the user asks for a "security review", "check this for vulnerabilities", "is this endpoint safe" or "audit the auth code", on a change touching input handling, authentication, secrets, file or network access or dependencies. Do not use for a full penetration test, a compliance audit, or changes that cross no trust boundary.

### `test-first-change`

Use when the user asks to "add this feature with tests", "write the test first", "fix this bug and add a regression test" or "do TDD", in code that automated tests can cover. Do not use for throwaway spikes, copy or config edits, generated code, or when the expected behavior or the cause of a failure is still unknown (use debug-from-evidence).

### `write-feature-spec`

Use when the user asks to "write a spec", "write a design doc", "spec this feature out" or "turn this into requirements", for a clarified feature over about one day or touching more than one team. Do not use for one-line fixes or spikes, an HTTP API contract (use design-http-api), or while blocking questions are still open (run clarify-requirements first).

### `write-incident-postmortem`

Use when the user asks to "write the postmortem", "write up the outage", "do a blameless review" or "document what happened in the incident", after it is mitigated. Do not use during live incident response (mitigate first), or to judge an individual's performance.

### `write-technical-docs`

Use when the user asks to "write a README", "document this", "write a runbook", "write a how-to" or "write a setup guide" that other people will follow. Do not use for inline code comments alone, marketing copy, or generated API reference, a feature spec (use write-feature-spec) or an incident write-up (use write-incident-postmortem).
